content: The axilla, commonly referred to as the armpit, underarm, or oxter, is the anatomical region located beneath the joint where the arm connects to the shoulder. Underarm hair typically begins to grow in both males and females during adolescence. In contemporary Western societies, it is customary for women to remove underarm hair for aesthetic purposes, while men generally retain it. However, some women, influenced by movements such as feminism, the hippie culture, or the punk rock scene, choose to keep their underarm hair for reasons ranging from personal comfort to challenging societal norms or promoting gender equality. Recently, an increasing number of men in the United States and Europe have started removing underarm hair, influenced by trends set by hairless male models and athletes, as well as a desire to avoid embarrassment when wearing sleeveless clothing. Body odor in the underarm region arises partly due to the metabolic byproducts of microorganisms that consume sebum, the fatty secretions produced by apocrine glands. To address this odor, a wide range of deodorants and antiperspirants are available on the market. Culturally, the underarms are one of the most sensitive areas of the human body to tickling. Additionally, sexual attraction to the underarm region is referred to as axillism. The term oxter, pronounced ock-ster, is predominantly used in Scotland, northern England, and Ireland, where it often replaces other terms for the underarm. The term underarm specifically refers to the external surface of the axilla, though it is frequently used interchangeably with armpit in casual language. Colloquially, armpit may also describe a place or object that is unpleasant, dirty, or undesirable. Several anatomical images are associated with the axilla, including depictions of the superficial muscles of the chest and arm, the axillary artery and its branches, the anterior view of the right upper limb and thorax, the veins of the right axilla, the infraclavicular portion of the right brachial plexus within the axillary fossa, and the left side of the thorax.
